p1.title: Passage 1
paras: The advent of CRISPR-Cas9 and advanced biomedicines marks a watershed moment in human history, offering the god-like power to edit the genetic code itself. We stand on the precipice of eradicating hereditary diseases like cystic fibrosis and sickle cell anemia. However, this scientific velocity outpaces our ethical frameworks. The prospect of “designer babies,” where genetic editing extends beyond therapy to enhancement (intelligence, physical traits), threatens to bifurcate humanity into biological castes. Furthermore, the exorbitant cost of personalized immunotherapies creates a chasm of inequality; biomedicine risks becoming a luxury good rather than a universal right. Unless regulatory bodies enforce equitable access and strict ethical boundaries, biotechnology could paradoxically exacerbate the human suffering it aims to alleviate by entrenching socio-economic disparities at a cellular level.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: The Indian Premier League (IPL) has transcended the boundaries of a mere sporting tournament to become a colossal socio-economic phenomenon. While purists lament the “Disneyfication” of the gentleman’s game—citing the erosion of technical finesse in favor of brute force and theatrics—the league’s economic footprint is undeniable. It has democratized cricket remuneration, pulling obscure domestic talents from hinterlands into the limelight of financial security. However, this commercial juggernaut raises pertinent questions regarding the commodification of national sentiment. The franchise model, heavily borrowed from American sports, risks diluting regional loyalties in favor of corporate identities. Furthermore, the relentless schedule contributes to player burnout, often rendering national duty secondary to contractual obligations. The challenge lies in balancing this commercial vitality with the sanctity of the sport, ensuring that the spectacle does not cannibalize the very skill set it intends to celebrate.

questions.q: The phrase “bifurcate humanity into biological castes” suggests
opts: a split between healthy and sick
a divide between the genetically enhanced wealthy and the unedited poor
a split between humans and AI
questions.why: Enhancement for those who can pay creates two biological classes. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Scientific Officer), Mar 2026.

questions.q: What is the “watershed moment” mentioned in the passage?
opts: the development of gene-editing technologies like CRISPR
questions.why: First sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Scientific Officer), Mar 2026.

questions.q: The author’s attitude towards biotechnology is
opts: cautiously hopeful but deeply concerned about ethics and equity
questions.why: Hope of curing disease, weighed against ethics and cost. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Scientific Officer), Mar 2026.

questions.q: Which is NOT mentioned as a risk of biomedicine?
questions.why: Weapons are never mentioned. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Scientific Officer), Mar 2026.

questions.q: What does the “chasm of inequality” refer to?
opts: the gap in access to advanced treatments due to high cost
questions.why: Caused by “the exorbitant cost of personalized immunotherapies”. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Scientific Officer), Mar 2026.

questions.q: The author’s use of the term “Disneyfication” implies
opts: the sport has become more child-friendly
the game is being trivialised into entertainment at the cost of technical quality
the league is owned by media conglomerates
questions.why: Purists cite “erosion of technical finesse in favor of brute force and theatrics”. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Mamlatdar / Vigilance Officer), Mar 2026.

questions.q: According to the passage, a positive outcome of the IPL is that
opts: it put national duty above contracts
it gave financial security to lesser-known domestic players
questions.why: Third sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Mamlatdar / Vigilance Officer), Mar 2026.

questions.q: The central conflict discussed in the passage is between

questions.why: Last sentence: “commercial vitality” vs “sanctity of the sport”. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Mamlatdar / Vigilance Officer), Mar 2026.

to promote to a new audience

questions.q: Choose the correct option: “It is high time we ______ the old files.”

questions.q: Choose the correct negative transformation: “Only a fool would say that.”
opts: Only not a fool would say that.
A fool would not say that.
Not a fool would say that.
None but a fool would say that.
questions.why: 'Only' = 'none but' (keeps the meaning). GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Select the correct indirect speech: He said, “Let us wait for the doctor.”
opts: He told to wait for the doctor.
He suggested that let them wait for the doctor.
He suggested that they should wait for the doctor.
He said that let us wait for the doctor.
questions.why: 'Let us' becomes 'suggested/proposed that they should'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: X, Y and Z start a firm with ₹90,000, ₹1,20,000 and ₹1,50,000. X, the managing partner, gets an allowance of ₹4,000 a month. Z's share of the divisible profit is guaranteed to be at least ₹1,15,000, any shortfall being borne by Y alone. If the annual profit before X's allowance is ₹2,88,000, what does Y finally receive?
questions.why: Allowance 48,000; divisible 2,40,000 in 3:4:5 gives 60,000 / 80,000 / 1,00,000. Z is 15,000 short, which Y pays: 80,000 − 15,000 = 65,000. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2026.

questions.q: Two ships on opposite sides of a 100 m lighthouse see its top at elevations of 30° and 45°. How far apart are the ships?
questions.why: Distances are 100√3 ≈ 173 m and 100 m; on opposite sides they add to about 273 m. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2025.

questions.q: Ayesha's father was 38 when she was born; her mother was 36 when her brother, four years younger than Ayesha, was born. What is the difference between the parents' ages?
questions.why: When Ayesha was born her mother was 36 − 4 = 32 and her father 38: a gap of 6 years. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2025.

questions.q: Four boxes each hold the same number of sweets and carry these labels: 'Five or Six', 'Seven or Eight', 'Six or Seven', 'Seven or Five'. Only one label is correct. How many sweets are in each box?
questions.why: Five, six and seven each make two labels true. Eight makes only 'Seven or Eight' true. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: A clock shows 4:30. It is placed so that the minute hand points east. In which direction does the hour hand point?
questions.why: At 4:30 the minute hand is at 6. If 6 points east, then 3 points north, and the hour hand, between 4 and 5, points north-east.

questions.q: A petroleum product's price rises 25% every odd year and falls 20% every even year. After exactly 8 years the price has
questions.why: × 1.25 × 0.8 = × 1 every two years, so after 8 years it is unchanged. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: A shoe showroom earns 25% profit after a 25% discount. What would the profit be with only a 10% discount?
questions.why: Marked 100 → sells 75 = 1.25 × cost → cost 60. At 90: profit 30 on 60 = 50%. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: Looking at a portrait, Arun said, 'I have no brother or sister, but this man's father is my father's son.' Whose portrait is it?
questions.why: With no brother, 'my father's son' is Arun himself. So Arun is the father of the man in the portrait.

questions.q: Numbers: 325 618 378 461 782 562 213. If the 1st and 3rd digits of each are interchanged, what is the sum of the product of the 1st and 3rd digits of the lowest number and that of the highest number?
questions.why: New numbers: 523 816 873 164 287 265 312. Lowest 164 → 1 × 4 = 4; highest 873 → 8 × 3 = 24; total 28. GPSC CBRT, Mar 2025.

questions.q: The first edition of the Organon (1810) was titled:
opts: Organon of the Healing Art (Organon der Heilkunst)
Organon of Rational Medicine (Organon der rationellen Heilkunde)
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. From the second edition (1819) the title became Organon der Heilkunst, Organon of the Healing Art.

questions.q: Hahnemann advised (§236) that in intermittent fevers the remedy is best given:
opts: at the height of the chill
immediately or very soon after the paroxysm ends
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. So that it can act before the next paroxysm.

questions.q: According to Hahnemann, emotional diseases of recent origin produced and kept up by the mind (§226) may be cured by:
opts: psychological means such as confidence, friendly advice and reasoning
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Psychotherapeutic measures, with a suitable antipsoric regimen afterwards.

questions.q: Homesickness with red cheeks, burning pains like pepper and chilliness in fat, flabby people suggests:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Capsicum: nostalgia with red face; burning like cayenne.

questions.q: Breathlessness with great rattling of mucus, worse at 3 a.m., in fat, sluggish patients with a tendency to cyanosis, suggests:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Ammonium carb: emphysema, weak heart, worse 3 a.m.

questions.q: Varicose veins, bone affections and complaints that are better from cold and worse from heat, in a syphilitic constitution, suggest:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Fluoric acid: warm-blooded, varicosities, bone decay.

questions.q: A patient who is very awkward, drops things, with puffiness and a tendency for marks to persist after pressure from scissors or instruments, suggests:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Bovista: awkwardness, deep imprints from blunt instruments.

questions.q: Under the old Hahnemannian method, mother tinctures were prepared in different classes according to:
opts: the juice and moisture content of the plant (Classes I to IX)
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. The new HPI method uses a uniform drug strength.

questions.q: For the 50 millesimal potencies Hahnemann medicated very small globules, about the size of:
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. 100 such globules weigh about one grain.

questions.q: Boenninghausen's first repertory, published in 1832, dealt with:
questions.why: 'Systematic Alphabetic Repertory of the Antipsoric Medicines' (1832); the non-antipsorics followed in 1835.

questions.q: Boenninghausen's Therapeutic Pocket Book was edited in English in 1891 by:
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. Timothy F. Allen's edition is the one in common use.

questions.q: The normal serum anion gap is about:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. Raised in diabetic ketoacidosis, lactic acidosis, renal failure and some poisonings.

questions.q: The baroreceptors that regulate blood pressure are located mainly in the:
questions.why: Carotid and aortic bodies are chemoreceptors.

questions.q: Lines of Zahn indicate:
opts: a thrombus formed in flowing blood (ante-mortem)
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Alternating platelet–fibrin and red-cell layers.

questions.q: The 'Tzanck smear' showing multinucleated giant cells is used to diagnose:
opts: herpes virus infections such as chickenpox
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. A bedside test.

questions.q: Asthma with suffocation from the slightest motion, relieved by being fanned, and a craving for fresh air suggests:
questions.why: Carbo veg's air hunger: 'wants to be fanned'.

questions.q: The investigation of choice for acute subarachnoid haemorrhage is (GPSC Medical Officer, 2025):
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Lumbar puncture for xanthochromia only if CT is negative.

questions.q: The most important mechanism in GERD is (GPSC Medical Officer, 2024):
opts: frequent transient lower oesophageal sphincter relaxations
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Transient LES relaxations allow reflux.

questions.q: The commonest heart defect in congenital rubella syndrome is (GPSC Medical Officer, 2024):
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Rubella triad: PDA, cataract, deafness.

questions.q: Physiological jaundice in a term newborn usually disappears by:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Prolonged jaundice needs evaluation.

questions.q: A whitish membrane on the tonsils that bleeds when scraped off suggests (GPSC Medical Officer, 2025):
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. The diphtheria pseudomembrane is adherent and bleeds on removal.

questions.q: Burns of the face and neck are dangerous mainly because of:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Early airway assessment is vital.

questions.q: 'Tache noire' is a post-mortem sign seen:
opts: on the skin of the back
in the eyes when the eyelids remain open
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Brownish-black discoloration of the exposed sclera.

questions.q: Under the National Commission for Homoeopathy Act, 2020, the National Register of homoeopathic practitioners is maintained by the:
opts: Medical Assessment and Rating Board for Homoeopathy
Board of Ethics and Registration for Homoeopathy
Central Council for Research in Homoeopathy
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. The NCH Act 2020 replaced the HCC Act 1973 and set up three autonomous boards.

questions.q: Euthanasia (passive) in India was permitted with safeguards following the Supreme Court judgment in:
opts: Common Cause v. Union of India (2018)
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. Also recognised living wills.
